correctness.rationale: The scalar fourth-power remainder is an exact nonnegative identity; summing it yields the uniform quartic support gap. A uniform fourth-order angular Laplace upper bound proves the global tilted-lattice summability exactly for p>7/4. An explicit N-axis strip yields power divergence below and logarithmic divergence at the boundary. The boundary endpoint lattice Riemann sum equals Γ(1/4)/(√2 a^(1/4)); two endpoints double it, while interior and exterior contributions are bounded. The Fourier Hilbert multiplication bound follows from coefficient Cauchy–Schwarz; no necessity of Hilbert multiplication failure is asserted. The standalone finite checker passed, independently of the proof.

value.rationale: The exact two-dimensional quartic spectral ball is a canonical uniformly convex norm with a fourth-order flat axial tangent. The result isolates a non-Euclidean shift of the natural subconvolution (and RKHS algebra sufficiency) boundary from the standard two-dimensional Euclidean exponent 3/2 to 7/4, and computes the exact critical logarithmic coefficient. The infinite structural threshold and coefficient are motivated by analytic multiplication stability, not by an arbitrary finite cutoff.
